LMGTE.title: Bertolini passes Kessel’s Ferrari on the last lap to win LMGTE
LMGTE.dek: Bertolini, Zlobin and Shaitar won for SMP Racing by passing the long-time leading Kessel Ferrari of Kemenater and Cressoni on the final lap, with JMW third.

facts.v: Bertolini caught the leading Kessel Ferrari with about a minute left and squeezed through at Piratella on the final lap.

chapters.title: A Ferrari field with SMP out for revenge
text: Fourteen LMGTE cars lined up at Imola for the second round, and nine of them were Ferrari 458 Italias, run by SMP Racing, Kessel Racing, AF Corse, JMW, AT Racing and Sofrev-ASP. Four Porsches and a single Aston Martin made up the rest. The opener at Silverstone had gone to AF Corse’s Griffin and Cameron after a close duel with SMP, and Bertolini and Shaitar arrived in Italy intent on revenge on AF Corse’s home ground.

Practice suggested they had the speed. Bertolini topped the opening session in the SMP Ferrari #72 on 1:41.649, three tenths ahead of Kessel’s #80, and improved to 1:40.620 in the afternoon, again narrowly ahead of the #80. Ferraris held the top seven places in the second session. In the AF Corse camp, Venturi had been drafted into the #55 alongside Griffin and Cameron, and JMW arrived on Michelin tyres after years on Dunlop. The Porsches were expected to suit the tight layout better than the Ferraris, but not to be able to match them over four hours.

chapters.title: Cressoni takes pole for Kessel
text: Cressoni set the pace in the 20-minute session, going round in 1:39.920 in the Kessel Ferrari #81 he shares with Kemenater. That was a little over three tenths clear of Bertolini’s SMP car on 1:40.221. Cioci was third in the first of AF Corse’s Ferraris, the #54, in a session that was interrupted by stoppages, including one that sent Cioci into the gravel at Tamburello.

Piccini recovered from an off to take fourth for Kessel’s second car, the #80, ahead of Griffin in the #55, Kaffer in the AT Racing Ferrari and Giammaria in AF Corse’s #65. JMW’s Zampieri lined up eighth after running wide over the kerbs at Variante Alta, with Ayari ninth for Sofrev-ASP. The best of the Porsches, Carroll in the Gulf car #86, was tenth, more than two seconds slower than the pole time.

chapters.title: Kessel runs away
text: The Kessel #81 was the class of the field in the opening stints. Once the race settled down it pulled out a lead of well over half a minute by the first round of scheduled stops, and the yellow Ferrari led for the majority of the afternoon. Behind it SMP’s #72 moved up and down the top six as Zlobin and Shaitar took the early stints, leaving Bertolini to do his work later in the race.

chapters.title: Safety car resets the gap
text: A safety car with roughly 90 minutes to run, called for damage to track furniture at Acque Minerale, bunched the field. The #81 still held a significant lead afterwards, but the SMP #72 was now in the hunt and gradually pulled it in. JMW’s #66 stayed in the mix for a podium for most of the race: McKenzie ran a strong opening stint, Richardson a mature middle one, and Zampieri then settled the car into the final podium place.

chapters.title: Bertolini catches Kessel at Tosa
text: Bertolini took over the SMP Ferrari for the last stint with a gap to close, and he steadily reeled in the Kessel car. With about a minute left he was on the back of it at Tosa. Kessel defended hard, but on the final lap Bertolini squeezed down the inside at Piratella and took the lead. The #81 finished second on the same lap, while JMW’s Ferrari took the last podium place.

chapters.title: SMP’s class win and a Ferrari sweep
text: The #72 of Bertolini, Zlobin and Shaitar won on 134 laps, with Kessel’s #81 of Kemenater and Cressoni second on the same lap and JMW’s #66 of McKenzie, Richardson and Zampieri third, also on 134. AT Racing’s #56 of the two Talkanitsas and Kaffer was fourth, one lap down, and Sofrev-ASP’s #58 of Barthez, Pons and Ayari fifth, so Ferraris swept the top five. IMSA Performance Matmut’s Porsche #76 was the best of the rest in sixth, two laps off, ahead of the AF Corse #55 of Cameron, Griffin and Venturi, which set the class fastest lap of 1:41.024. Kessel’s #80 and AF Corse’s #54 were not classified.
The ELMS next travels to the Red Bull Ring on 20 July, where Griffin and Cameron, the Silverstone winners, will look to hit back.

GTC.title: Mac turns a surprise pole into Formula Racing’s GTC win
GTC.dek: Laursen, Mac and Piccini won GTC for Formula Racing from pole, holding off the SMP Racing Ferraris of Beretta and Persiani, who took second and third.

facts.v: Mac put the Formula Racing Ferrari on pole by just under three tenths, quick enough to sit between GTE cars on the grid.

chapters.title: Ferraris in force, Team Ukraine absent
text: Fourteen GTC cars were in the Imola results, and Ferrari 458 Italia GT3s dominated them. SMP Racing ran three, the #57, #71 and #73, with team principal Rotenberg, absent from Silverstone, in the #57 line-up. AF Corse ran four of its own, and the Formula Racing entry was run by AF Corse with Piccini standing in for Jan Magnussen. Team Ukraine, winner of the Silverstone opener, withdrew without an official reason being given, which removed the main rival to SMP.

The non-Ferrari challenge came from ART Grand Prix’s two McLarens, Pro GT by Almeras’ Porsche and the Team Russia by Barwell BMW. Perera was vocal that the balance of performance favoured the Ferraris on a track where AF Corse had tested a lot, and Almeras’ Porsche was within two tenths of the SMP pace in the opening session. That session was led by Beretta in the #73 on 1:43.365, and the #71 of Ladygin, Basov and Persiani, which had retired at Silverstone after taking pole, topped the second.

chapters.title: Mac on a surprise pole
text: Mac took a surprise pole, setting 1:42.082 in the Formula Racing Ferrari #60. That was just under three tenths ahead of the AF Corse #95 of Sbirrazzuoli and de Leener, and fast enough to split a group of LMGTE cars on the overall grid. Mac’s previous GT3 experience at the track amounted to a 20-lap test earlier that year.

Persiani put the #71 third on 1:42.691, ahead of Korjus in the ART McLaren #98 on 1:42.696, with Beretta’s #73 fifth, Perera’s Porsche sixth and Castellacci’s AF Corse #94 seventh. Brundle in the second McLaren was eighth. The slowest two cars, AF Corse’s #63 and Sofrev-ASP’s #59, were more than four seconds off the pole time.

chapters.title: SMP and AF Corse trade the lead
text: Laursen started from pole for Formula Racing, and for much of the afternoon the class lead moved among several Ferraris. Beretta held it at stages for SMP, as did Kirill Ladygin in the sister #71 and Castellacci in the AF Corse #94. A safety car after about two and a half hours bunched up the field. Behind the Ferraris, ART’s McLaren #99 of Brundle, Ajlani and Gonzalez fought its way up to fourth in class.

chapters.title: Mac holds on for Formula Racing
text: Mac, who had put the car on pole, was the standout of Formula Racing’s trio. He gave the team the foundation for the win by fending off the more experienced Beretta and Persiani, and the Dane brought the #60 home without any major problem. SMP’s #73 and #71 finished second and third on the same lap.

chapters.title: Formula Racing take the points lead
text: The #60 of Laursen, Mac and Piccini won on 132 laps, with SMP Racing’s #73 of Beretta, Markozov and Anton Ladygin second and the #71 of Kirill Ladygin, Basov and Persiani third, both on the same lap. The best non-Ferrari was ART’s McLaren #99, fourth in class three laps down, ahead of Sofrev-ASP’s #59 and AF Corse’s #63. Castellacci’s #94 set the class fastest lap, 1:43.035, but finished seventh. Brundle said the McLaren’s pit stops cost at least a minute over four visits because of its fuel-flow timing, which he called a handicap for the car. Prospeed’s Porsche #75 was not classified.
Mac said the team had done the job as planned with no real issues, after a tough Silverstone. The series moves on to the Red Bull Ring on 20 July.
